A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Omni-Scene work. All 18 pages of each version, including the seven-page supplementary material, provide readable text, equations, figures and tables supporting comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original reconstruction experiments on nuScenes and RealEstate10K, component ablations, runtime measurements and bin-size generalization results.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and qualitative generation demonstrations, with revised numerical results for Omni-Scene on nuScenes.

M1.justification: The Volume Builder, Pixel Decorator, feature fusion, depth initialization and training losses remain unchanged. CIDA/CPDA terminology and revised diagrams clarify the existing attention mechanisms without changing their procedures.

E1.justification: Both versions retain nuScenes ego-centric reconstruction, RealEstate10K scene-centric reconstruction and text/layout-conditioned scene generation. The supplementary evaluations at different bin sizes and qualitative challenging conditions also remain.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged: pixelSplat and MVSplat, the additional AttnRend and MuRF comparisons in Tables 1 and 4, and MagicDrive3D in Figure 6. The newly cited Lift-Splat-Shoot is discussed rather than evaluated.

E3.justification: Reported splits, six input and twelve target views, image resolution, metrics and training budgets remain unchanged. Supplementary Section 7.5 retains the same bin sizes and 50,000-step fine-tuning protocol.

E4.justification: Quantitative evidence within existing analyses is revised. The updated full-model reference changes the component-ablation gaps in Section 4.3, while Table 6 revises bin-size generalization results. No new ablation, robustness condition or case study is introduced.

E5.justification: Both retain runtime averaging over 2,048 measurements and the same generation seed labels. Neither adds training-run counts, confidence intervals, error bars or significance testing.

E6.justification: Tables 1, 2 and 4 revise Omni-Scene's nuScenes PSNR/SSIM/LPIPS/PCC from 24.01/0.733/0.238/0.804 to 24.27/0.736/0.237/0.800. Table 6 also changes, including 6.4m PSNR without fine-tuning from 22.65 to 22.89. Baseline scores, RealEstate10K results and overall rankings remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(4) retain their mathematical content. Renaming attention outputs from Img/Plane to CIDA/CPDA is notational; no definitions, assumptions, derivations or proofs are substantively revised.

C1.justification: The reconstruction and generation claims retain their meaning and scope. Although generation is removed from the abstract and introductory contribution list, its pioneering feed-forward generation claim is restated in Section 4.2 and generation remains in the conclusion.

C2.justification: The new Section 2 paragraph explicitly argues that low-resolution volumes suffice for coarse 3D perception but cannot meet fine-grained reconstruction requirements. This extends the applicability explanation; existing experimental interpretations and failure-case discussions remain.

D1.justification: Sections 4.1 and 6, including Table 3, retain the same preprocessing instructions, architecture parameters, loss weights, hardware and training settings. The project URL and supplementary-material access information are unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds a focused discussion of neural representations in 3D perception and a new Lift-Splat-Shoot citation. It expands comparisons with BEV and occupancy methods already cited; the remaining reference changes are renumbering.

P1.justification: v2 expands related work and the attention explanation, introduces CIDA/CPDA abbreviations, and redistributes the generation contribution wording. These are localized edits within the existing document organization.

P2.justification: Figures 2 and 3 revise schematic details, particularly the triplane-attention illustration and labels. The remaining figures and table structures are retained, with limited layout adjustments and text reflow.

improvement.justification: The expanded comparison with 3D-perception methods and more explicit attention diagram modestly improve the explanation of the design and its research context. Experimental coverage and methodology remain stable. The mixed numerical revisions do not independently establish stronger validation, so the overall gain is limited to explanation and presentation.
